description: The knot, and then a knife

participation.context: Brought the parcel, refused the child's name, and read the slip.
participation.name: William Shakespeare

participation.context: Tried fingers, teeth, a fork, and a speech, and did not get the name.
participation.name: Will Kemp

participation.context: Produced a knife without being asked, and ended it in one stroke.
participation.name: Alice Brambleby

participation.context: Her hand on the slip, and nothing on it but whom.
participation.name: Susanna Shakespeare

participation.context: The cake is hers. She is not at the table.
participation.name: Mary Shakespeare

relations.note: a knife ends what a speech is enjoying

story.body: You would not carry the household joke out of Henley Street. Kemp had the fork in the knot. Alice cut it. You read the slip and stopped at whom.

relations.note: a knife ends what a speech is enjoying

title: Alice ended the knot with a knife

participation.context: Looked, and did not pick the fork out.
participation.name: William Shakespeare

participation.context: His fork still in the knot. He is not in the picture.
participation.name: Will Kemp

story.body: You kept the cut knot, the hose, and the fork. You left the faces out.

title: Left Kemp's fork in the cut knot

participation.context: Named for the hand, and not for the knot.
participation.name: Susanna Shakespeare

story.body: You kept the slip to the word whom, in Susanna's hand. The promise held, and you did not name the child.

title: Kept Susanna's slip to the word whom
